[LSTR.11.3] A value longer than its slot's `capacity` that reaches the slot
at run time, in an asserted fact or an emitted one, is a bounds refusal
([LERR.1.5]). The engine must not store it: the assert or the emit does not
happen, and the `BoundsError` names `CAP_VALUE_CAPACITY` ([RTCT.7.1]), with the
capacity as its limit and the value's length as the observed count. A refused
emit stops its firing there: the actions after it do not run ([LERR.1.5]). In a `FactExternal`, at any depth,
it refuses the whole record, and that status is the whole refusal: there is no
`BoundsError` ([NCBK.10.4]).

The engine must not truncate the value instead. A shortened string is a
different value, and every equality over the slot would silently change.
